A flat stone by a stream
82300.e: A rock face is a steep, often almost vertical surface of rock. You find them on many mountains.
82300.m: A rock face is a steep slope of rock.

82301.q: Which famous rock face is in the Bernese Oberland?
82301.e: The Eiger North Face is about 1800 metres high. It is one of the best-known climbing walls in the Alps.
82301.m: The Eiger North Face is a famous rock face.

82302.q: Who climbs rock faces with a rope and a helmet?
82302.e: Climbers go up rock faces with a rope, harness and helmet. The rope protects them if they fall.
82302.m: Climbers secure themselves on the rock face with a rope.

82303.q: Which big bird of prey often builds its nest on rock faces?
82303.e: The golden eagle likes to build its eyrie on steep rock faces. There it is safe from enemies.
82303.m: The golden eagle likes to nest on rock faces.

82304.q: In which valley do the Staubbach Falls plunge over a high rock face?
82304.e: The Lauterbrunnen valley has very steep rock faces. Lots of waterfalls plunge down them, for example the Staubbach Falls.
82304.m: The Lauterbrunnen valley has high rock faces and waterfalls.

82305.q: Why do you need to be careful at the foot of a rock face?
a: The ground is made of glass
82305.e: Stones keep coming loose from a rock face. That is why it is dangerous at the foot of the face.
82305.m: Stones can fall down below rock faces.

82306.q: What is an easy climbing route with fixed steel cables and ladders called?
82306.e: On a via ferrata, steel cables, rungs and ladders are fixed to the rock. You clip yourself in with a special set and are protected that way.
82306.m: A via ferrata has fixed steel cables on the rock.

82307.q: Which animal with big curved horns climbs skilfully on rock faces?
82307.e: The ibex has hooves that grip well on rock. It climbs safely over steep rocks.
82307.m: The ibex climbs skilfully on rock.

82308.e: In a rockfall, stones come loose from a slope or a rock face. They fall or bounce down.

82309.q: What protects your head from falling stones when climbing?
82309.e: A hard helmet stops falling stones. That is why climbers and mountaineers wear a helmet.
82309.m: A helmet protects your head from falling stones.

82310.q: What is put up along mountain roads to protect cars from falling stones?
82310.e: Strong steel nets catch falling stones. That keeps roads and railway lines safer.

a: When ice in the rock thaws
When there is no wind in winter
When it has been dry for a long time
At night during a full moon
82311.e: Ice holds loose stones in place like glue. When it thaws, the stones come loose and fall down.
82311.m: There is often rockfall when things thaw.

82312.q: What should you shout if you kick a stone loose yourself?
82312.e: By shouting “Rock!” loudly, you warn people further down. Then they can protect themselves.
82312.m: If you kick a stone loose, shout “Rock!” loudly.

82313.q: What does a road sign with falling stones on it show?
82313.e: The sign warns of stones that can fall onto the road. You should not stop there.
82313.m: The sign with falling stones warns of rockfall.

82314.q: How should you behave on a path where there is a danger of falling rocks?
a: Stop for a long time and have a picnic
82314.e: Where stones can fall, you do not stand still. You keep walking briskly until you are out of the danger zone.
82314.m: Do not take a break in rockfall zones.

82315.q: What is a roof over a road called that protects it from stones and avalanches?
82315.e: A gallery is a strong concrete roof over the road, closed on the mountain side. Stones and avalanches slide over the top of it.
82315.m: A gallery protects roads from stones and avalanches.

a: A large area of lying snow
An ice rink in the village
82316.e: A snowfield is a large area of snow in the mountains. It often stays until well into the summer.
82316.m: A snowfield is a large area of snow in the mountains.

82317.q: Why is there still snow on high mountains even in summer?
a: Because it is colder up there
Because the sun does not shine there
Because the snow there is salty
82317.e: The higher you go, the colder it gets. That is why the snow melts more slowly up there and stays.
82317.m: It is colder high up, so the snow stays longer.

82318.q: Why is a steep snowfield dangerous when hiking?
82318.e: Snow can be hard and slippery. If you slip, you can slide down the slope.
82318.m: You can slip on steep snowfields.

82319.q: How does old snow on a snowfield often feel in spring?
82319.e: Old snow thaws during the day and freezes again at night. This makes it grainy and wet.

82320.q: What can form from snowfields over many years?
82320.e: If snow stays every year, it gets pressed into ice under its own weight. This is how a glacier can form.
82320.m: Snow that stays can turn into a glacier.

82321.q: What protects your eyes on a bright snowfield?
82321.e: It is very glaring on a snowfield. Good sunglasses protect your eyes from the strong light.

82322.q: What does the meltwater from snowfields do in summer?
82322.e: In summer the snow melts slowly. The water flows into streams, rivers and lakes.
82322.m: Meltwater fills the streams in summer.

82323.q: Why do you get sunburnt quickly on snowfields?
82323.e: The bright snow strongly reflects the sunlight. That is why almost twice as much light hits your skin, and you need sun cream.
82323.m: On snow you need sun cream.

a: A deep shaft in the glacier ice
82324.e: A glacier mill is a round, deep shaft in the ice of a glacier. Meltwater swirls down it into the depths.
82324.m: A glacier mill is a shaft in the glacier ice.

82325.q: What grinds a round hole into the rock at the bottom of a glacier mill?
a: Swirling water with sand and stones
82325.e: The water plunges through the glacier mill right down to the rock. There it swirls sand and gravel round and round and so grinds out a round hole.
82325.m: Swirling water with sand and stones grinds round holes into the rock.

82326.q: Why is a glacier mill called a “mill”?
a: The water turns and grinds inside it
Flour used to be ground there
It has sails like a windmill
82326.e: In a glacier mill, the water swirls round and grinds sand and stones. That is like a mill.
82326.m: In a glacier mill, the water turns like in a mill.

82327.q: What often lies right at the bottom of a glacier pothole?
82327.e: The stones were turned round and round by the water for a long time. This ground them round and smooth.
82327.m: Round, smooth stones often lie in glacier potholes.

82328.q: What shape are the walls of a glacier mill?
82328.e: The swirling water melts and grinds the walls round and round. That is why they are round and smooth.
82328.m: Glacier mills have round, smooth walls.

82329.q: Why do you find round holes from glacier mills even where there is no glacier today?
a: There used to be a glacier there
82329.e: In the Ice Age there were glaciers in many places in Switzerland. When they melted, the round holes were left in the rock.
82329.m: Round holes in the rock show that there used to be a glacier there.

82330.q: Where does the water plunge to in a glacier mill?
a: Down to the rock bed under the glacier
82330.e: The meltwater flows over the ice into the glacier mill. Then it plunges down to the rock bed under the glacier.
82330.m: The water of a glacier mill plunges down to the rock bed.

82331.q: How long did the water take to grind a deep hole into the rock under a glacier mill?
82331.e: Rock is very hard. The water with sand and stones had to swirl round for a very long time before a deep hole formed.
82331.m: Deep holes in the rock took a long time to form.

82332.q: Which city is the well-known Glacier Garden in?
82332.e: The Glacier Garden is in Lucerne. There you can see traces of the Ice Age right in the middle of the city.
82332.m: The Glacier Garden is in Lucerne.

82333.q: What can you see in the rock at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne?
82333.e: In the Glacier Garden you can see big, round holes in the rock. These glacier potholes were drilled by the water of a glacier.
82333.m: You can see glacier potholes at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne.

82335.q: What was someone trying to build when the Glacier Garden was discovered?
82335.e: Josef Wilhelm Amrein-Troller wanted to dig a wine cellar. While digging, the glacier potholes came to light.
82335.m: The Glacier Garden was found while building a wine cellar.

82336.q: What can you get lost in at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne?
82336.e: At the Glacier Garden there is a maze with lots of mirrors. It is easy to get lost in it.
82336.m: There is a mirror maze at the Glacier Garden.

82337.q: Which famous monument with an animal is right next to the Glacier Garden?
82337.e: The Lion Monument is a dying lion carved into the rock. It is only a few steps away from the Glacier Garden.
82337.m: The Lion Monument is next to the Glacier Garden.

82338.q: What time do the glacier potholes in the Glacier Garden in Lucerne come from?
82338.e: The holes formed about 20,000 years ago. At that time it was much colder than today.
82338.m: The glacier potholes in Lucerne come from the Ice Age.

82339.q: What lay over today's city of Lucerne in the Ice Age?
82339.e: In the Ice Age the glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. There was thick ice over Lucerne too.
82339.m: In the Ice Age there was a glacier over Lucerne.

82340.q: In which Swiss city do two big erratic boulders, the Pierres du Niton, stick out of the lake?
82340.e: The two Pierres du Niton lie in the harbour of Geneva in Lake Geneva. A glacier carried them there from the Mont Blanc area in the Ice Age.
82340.m: The Pierres du Niton are in Geneva.

82341.q: Why is an erratic boulder called a “Findling” (foundling) in German?
a: It lies there out of place, as if found
82341.e: An erratic boulder is often made of a different rock from its surroundings. It lies there as if someone had put it down.
82341.m: An erratic boulder does not match the rock around it.

82342.q: Where in Switzerland can you find lots of erratic boulders?
82342.e: In the Ice Age the glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. That is why there are lots of erratic boulders there.
82342.m: There are lots of erratic boulders on the Central Plateau.

82343.q: What can experts tell from erratic boulders?
a: How far glaciers used to reach
82343.e: Glaciers carried the boulders to their edges. That is why erratic boulders show how far the ice used to reach.
82343.m: Erratic boulders show how far the glaciers used to reach.

82344.q: How big can erratic boulders be?
a: Only as big as a pea
Only as big as an egg
Only as big as an apple
82344.e: Some erratic boulders are huge and weigh many tonnes. Some are as big as a house.
82344.m: Some erratic boulders are as big as a house.

82345.q: What is the technical name for a boulder that a glacier carried far from its home?
82345.e: Erratic means “strayed”. Such a boulder is like a stone that has strayed and lies far away from its home.
82345.m: A boulder like this is called an erratic block.

82346.q: How long does it take for a glacier to carry an erratic boulder a long way?
82346.e: Glaciers usually only flow a few metres to a few hundred metres a year. So for a long journey they need many hundreds of years or even longer.
82346.m: Glaciers carry erratic boulders very slowly.

a: A lake high up in the mountains
82347.e: A mountain lake lies high up in the mountains. It is often small, cold and clear.
82347.m: A mountain lake lies high up in the mountains.

82348.q: Why is the water in mountain lakes usually very cold?
a: It comes from snow and glaciers
82348.e: Many mountain lakes are filled by meltwater. Also, it is cool high up, so the water stays cold.
82348.m: Mountain lakes are cold because meltwater flows into them.

82349.q: What carved out many of the hollows for mountain lakes?
82349.e: In the Ice Age, glaciers ground hollows into the rock. When the ice melted, these hollows filled with water.
82349.m: Many mountain lakes lie in hollows that glaciers ground out.

82350.q: Which village in the Bernese Oberland is the well-known Lake Oeschinen near?
82350.e: Lake Oeschinen lies above Kandersteg. It is surrounded by high rock faces.

82351.q: Why are the mountains often reflected so beautifully in a mountain lake?
a: The water is calm and clear
The water is full of foam
The lake is made of glass
There are mirrors in the lake
82351.e: When there is no wind, the surface of the water is as smooth as a mirror. That is why you can see the mountains in it.

82352.q: What colour are some mountain lakes because of fine rock flour?
82352.e: Fine rock flour from glaciers floats in the water. It scatters the light, and the lake shines turquoise.
82352.m: Rock flour makes some mountain lakes turquoise.

82353.q: Which fish often lives in cold, clear mountain lakes?
82353.e: Trout like cold water with lots of oxygen. That is why they like living in mountain lakes and mountain streams.
82353.m: Trout like living in cold mountain lakes.

82354.q: Which mountain is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze and has a famous pyramid shape?
82354.e: The Matterhorn also stands near Zermatt. It is world famous for its pointed pyramid shape, but it is lower than the Dufourspitze.
82354.m: The Matterhorn is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze.

82355.q: Which pass do you take from Tiefencastel into the Upper Engadine to St Moritz?
82355.e: The road over the Julier Pass leads from Tiefencastel to Silvaplana in the Upper Engadine. From there it is not far to St Moritz.
82355.m: The Julier Pass leads into the Upper Engadine.

82356.q: In old legends, who threw the erratic boulders around the countryside?
82356.e: In the past, people did not know that glaciers had brought the stones. That is why legends told of giants or the devil throwing them.
82356.m: In old legends, giants threw the erratic boulders.

82357.q: Which plants often grow on a scree slope?
82357.e: On a scree slope there is little soil and the stones move. Only a few tough plants with long roots can grow there.
82357.m: Only a few tough plants grow on scree slopes.

82358.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid water?
82358.e: When warm water vapour cools, little drops of water form again. This process is called condensation.
82358.m: In condensation, vapour turns back into water.

82359.q: What are the clouds in the sky made of?
a: Tiny drops of water and ice
82359.e: Clouds form when moist air rises and cools. This forms tiny drops of water or ice crystals.
82359.m: Clouds are made of very small drops of water or ice crystals.

82360.q: What are the drops of water that form on the grass early in the morning called?
82360.e: In the cool night, water vapour from the air turns into drops on the blades of grass. These drops are called dew.
82360.m: In the morning, dew often sparkles on the meadow.

82361.q: Why does a glass with an ice-cold drink get wet on the outside?
a: Water from the air settles on it
The glass has a tiny hole
The drink pushes through the glass
82361.e: The air contains invisible water vapour. On the cold glass it turns into drops.
82361.m: Drops of water from the air form on cold objects.

82362.q: Why do your glasses steam up in winter when you come into a warm house?
a: Warm, moist air cools on the cold lenses
The glasses get dirty in the house
The lenses go soft in the warmth
There is more dust in the house
82362.e: The glasses are still cold from outside. The warm room air cools on them, and its water vapour turns into tiny drops.
82362.m: Cold glasses steam up in a warm room.

82363.q: Why is the inside of the window panes often wet on cold winter mornings?
a: Moist room air cools on the glass
The cleaning cloth was too wet
82363.e: The warm air in the room contains water vapour. It cools on the cold pane, and drops form.
82363.m: Moisture collects on cold window panes.

82364.q: What are the white lines that aeroplanes draw high up in the sky called?
82364.e: The exhaust from the engines contains water vapour. In the freezing cold high up, it turns into tiny ice crystals that you see as lines.
82364.m: Condensation trails are made of tiny ice crystals.

82365.q: Why does water drip from the pipe of an air conditioner in summer?
a: Moisture from the air turns to water inside it
The unit is filled with water
The water comes from the rain
82365.e: In the air conditioner, the warm air is cooled down a lot. Its water vapour turns into water that has to drain away.
82365.m: When air cools a lot, its vapour turns into water.

82366.q: What is it called when water slowly turns into invisible vapour without boiling?
82366.e: Even without boiling, water particles are constantly passing into the air. This slow process is called evaporation.
82366.m: Water can evaporate even without boiling.

82368.q: Why do you feel cold when you climb out of the swimming pool wet?
a: The water on your skin evaporates and cools you
There are little bits of ice in the water
82368.e: Water needs heat to evaporate. It takes this heat from our skin, which is why we feel cold.

82369.q: Which cycle begins with water evaporating from seas and lakes?
82369.e: The evaporated water rises, forms clouds and falls back down as rain or snow. In this way the water keeps going round in a circle.
82369.m: In the water cycle, water travels between the earth and the sky.

82370.q: What provides most of the energy for water to evaporate from the sea?
82370.e: The sun warms the sea and the air. This makes a huge amount of water evaporate every day.
82370.m: The sun drives the evaporation of water.

82371.q: Why do people sometimes put a bowl of water on the radiator in winter?
a: To make the room air moister
82371.e: The warmth makes the water in the bowl evaporate. This puts more moisture into the dry heated air.
82371.m: Evaporating water makes dry air moister.

82372.q: How is salt obtained from seawater by the sea?
a: The water is left to evaporate in the sun
The water is shaken for a long time
The water is poured through a sieve
82372.e: In shallow pools, the sun and wind dry the seawater. The water goes into the air and the salt is left behind.
82372.m: When seawater evaporates, salt is left behind.

82373.q: How does a wet bath towel dry faster?
82373.e: Spread out, the towel has a large surface where water can go into the air. Scrunched up, it stays damp for a long time.
82373.m: A large surface makes water evaporate faster.

82374.q: On a high mountain, does water boil at more or less than 100 degrees?
a: It doesn't boil there at all
82374.e: On a mountain, less air presses down on the water. That is why it boils at a lower heat, for example at a mountain hut in the Alps.
82374.m: The higher you are, the sooner water boils.

82375.q: Which device do you use to measure how hot the water is?
82375.e: A thermometer shows the temperature. In Switzerland it is measured in degrees Celsius.
82375.m: You measure temperature with a thermometer.

a: The temperature at which something boils
The temperature at which something freezes
The highest point of a mountain
The point in the middle of the pan
82376.e: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil. For water at sea level, this is 100 degrees Celsius.
82376.m: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil.

82377.q: Who is the temperature unit degree Celsius named after?
82377.e: Anders Celsius was a scientist from Sweden. Almost 300 years ago he suggested a scale with 100 steps between water freezing and boiling.
82377.m: The Celsius scale is named after Anders Celsius.

82378.q: What happens to boiling water in an open pan if you turn the hob up even higher?
82378.e: The extra heat only makes more water turn to steam. But the temperature of the water does not rise above the boiling point.
82378.m: Boiling water does not get hotter, it just turns to steam faster.

82379.q: Why does water come to the boil faster with a lid on the pan?
a: The lid keeps the heat in the pan
The lid makes the water salty
The lid squeezes the water smaller
82379.e: Without a lid, a lot of heat escapes with the steam. With a lid, the heat stays in the pan, and you save energy too.
82379.m: With a lid, water boils faster and you save electricity.

82380.q: Which kitchen appliance boils water for tea especially quickly?
82380.e: In a kettle, a heating element warms the water directly. It switches itself off when the water boils.

82381.q: What is a pan with a tightly sealed lid, in which food cooks much faster, called?
82381.e: In a pressure cooker the steam cannot escape, so the pressure rises. This means the water only boils above 100 degrees, and the food cooks faster.
82381.m: It gets hotter in a pressure cooker than in an open pan.

82382.q: What happens to a puddle when it is minus 5 degrees outside?
82382.e: Minus 5 degrees is colder than the freezing point of water. That is why the puddle turns to ice.
82382.m: Below 0 degrees, a puddle turns to ice.

82383.q: Where in the kitchen do you keep food at about minus 18 degrees?
82383.e: A freezer keeps food at about minus 18 degrees. That way it keeps for a long time.
82383.m: It is much colder in the freezer than in the fridge.

82384.q: What are the balls of ice that sometimes fall from the sky in a thunderstorm called?
82384.e: In a thundercloud, drops of water freeze into balls of ice. When they fall, this is called hail.
82384.m: Hail is balls of ice from a thundercloud.

82385.q: Why should you never touch an ice-cold metal pole with your tongue in winter?
a: Your tongue can freeze to it
82385.e: The moist tongue cools down instantly on the ice-cold metal. The moisture freezes and the tongue sticks fast.

82386.q: What does it mean when the thermometer shows ‘minus 10 degrees’?
82386.e: The minus shows temperatures below zero. So minus 10 degrees is 10 degrees colder than 0 degrees.
82386.m: Minus degrees are colder than zero degrees.

82387.q: Why do people put antifreeze in the water for the car windscreen in winter?
82387.e: With antifreeze, the water only freezes at much lower temperatures. So you can clean the windscreen in winter too.

82388.q: What do you call it when rain freezes at once into a slippery layer of ice on the cold ground?
82388.e: When rain falls on ground colder than 0 degrees, it turns to ice at once. Then roads and pavements are very slippery.
82388.m: With black ice, the pavement is very slippery.

82389.q: What do you call weather with temperatures below 0 degrees?
82389.e: When it is colder than 0 degrees, we call it frost. Then water freezes outdoors.
82389.m: When there is frost, it is colder than zero degrees.

82390.q: Which three states can water have?
82390.e: Water can be solid as ice, liquid as water and a gas as steam. These are called states of matter.
82390.m: Water can be solid, liquid or gas.

82391.q: What state is an ice cube in?
82391.e: An ice cube is hard and keeps its shape. That is why it is solid.

82392.q: What state is water vapour in?
82392.e: Water vapour is a gas. It spreads out in the air and is invisible.
82392.m: Water vapour is water as a gas.

82393.q: What do you call it when ice turns into water?
82393.e: When ice gets warm, it becomes liquid. This process is called melting.
82393.m: When ice melts, it turns into water.

82394.q: What do you call it when a liquid becomes solid, for example hot wax?
82394.e: When a liquid cools, at some point it becomes solid. This process is called solidifying.
82394.m: When solidifying, a liquid becomes solid.

82395.q: What state is the lava that flows out of a volcano in?
82395.e: Lava is rock so hot that it flows. When it cools, it turns back into solid rock.

82396.q: What do you call it when water turns into steam while boiling?
82396.e: When boiling, liquid water quickly changes into a gas. This is called vaporising.
82396.m: When vaporising, a liquid turns into a gas.

82397.q: What shape are snowflakes when you look at them under a magnifying glass?
82397.e: Snowflakes are small ice crystals. They almost always have six arms or points.

82398.q: What happens to a blown-up balloon if you put it in the fridge?
82398.e: Cold air takes up less space than warm air. That is why the balloon shrinks a little.

82399.q: What can happen to a fully blown-up balloon in the hot sun?
82399.e: Warm air takes up more space. If the balloon is already full, the skin can tear.

82400.q: Why does an open balloon whizz around the room when you let go of it?
a: The air rushing out pushes it
It is pulled by the lamp
A gust of wind carries it
82400.e: The air rushes out of the back of the balloon. As it does, it pushes the balloon in the opposite direction. This is called recoil.
82400.m: Air rushing out drives a balloon forward.

82401.q: What are most balloons made of?
82401.e: Most balloons are made of rubber, or more exactly natural rubber. Rubber can stretch a lot.
82401.m: Balloons are made of stretchy rubber.

82402.q: Why does a balloon stick to the wall after you have rubbed it on your hair?
82402.e: When rubbed, the balloon gets an electric charge. This holds it to the wall.
82402.m: Rubbing gives a balloon an electric charge.

82403.q: Why does a helium balloon go limp after a few days?
a: The gas slowly escapes through the skin
82403.e: Helium particles are tiny. Little by little they slip out through the balloon skin.
82403.m: A helium balloon slowly loses its gas.

82404.q: Why does a balloon go bang when you prick it with a needle?
a: The air inside escapes all at once
82404.e: The air in the balloon is squashed together. When the skin tears, the air shoots out suddenly, and that makes the bang.
82404.m: A balloon goes bang because the air escapes suddenly.

82405.q: What happens if you blow up a balloon far too much?
82405.e: Rubber can only stretch up to a limit. If the skin gets too thin, it tears.
82405.m: A balloon blown up too much bursts.

82406.q: Why should you not leave bits of balloon lying around in nature?
82406.e: Birds, cows or wild animals sometimes mistake bits of balloon for food. This can make them ill.
82406.m: Bits of balloon belong in the bin.

82407.q: Which organ do we breathe with?
82407.e: Air goes through the nose or mouth into the lungs. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

82408.q: What do green plants give off into the air that we need to breathe?
82408.e: With the help of sunlight, plants make food from air and water. As they do, they give off oxygen, which we breathe in.
82408.m: Plants give off oxygen into the air.

82409.q: Why is the air we breathe out moist?
82409.e: In the lungs the air picks up moisture. That is why breathed-out air contains a lot of water vapour.

82410.q: Why should a classroom be aired regularly?
a: So that stale air gets out
So that the room gets darker
So that the floor gets clean
So that the lights shine brighter
82410.e: Lots of people in a room breathe out a lot of carbon dioxide. Airing lets fresh air in, and you can concentrate better.

82411.q: Through which part of the body is it best to breathe in, because it warms and cleans the air?
82411.e: In the nose the air is warmed and moistened. Tiny hairs hold back dust.
82411.m: The nose warms and cleans the air we breathe.

82412.q: What do divers need to be able to breathe underwater?
82412.e: A compressed air tank holds a lot of squashed-together air. The diver can breathe from it through a hose.
82412.m: Divers take their air with them in a tank.

82413.q: Which animal breathes underwater with gills?
82413.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. Dolphins and whales, on the other hand, breathe air at the surface with lungs.

82414.q: What is the tube called through which the air we breathe goes from the throat to the lungs?
82414.e: The windpipe leads from the throat down to the lungs. The gullet next to it takes food to the stomach.
82414.m: The air we breathe flows through the windpipe.

82415.q: Which gas makes the bubbles in fizzy mineral water?
82415.e: Carbon dioxide is pressed into mineral water, or it is already in the spring water. In water it is often called carbonic acid.
82415.m: The bubbles in mineral water are carbon dioxide.

82416.q: What happens when you open a fizzy drink bottle that has been shaken?
82416.e: Shaking forms lots of gas bubbles. When you open the bottle, they escape all at once and carry water with them.
82416.m: Shaken fizzy bottles spray when opened.

82417.q: Why does mineral water taste flat if the bottle has been left open for a long time?
82417.e: The carbon dioxide gradually escapes into the air as a gas. Then the water no longer tingles.
82417.m: Open fizzy water loses its bubbles.

82418.q: Which of these drinks normally has no fizz?
82418.e: Cola, lemonade and sparkling water contain carbon dioxide. Milk does not fizz.

82419.q: Where does the fizz stay in the water longer?
82419.e: Cold water can hold more gas than warm. That is why a cool mineral water stays fizzy longer.
82419.m: Cold fizzy water stays bubbly longer.

82420.q: What do you hear when you open a fizzy drink bottle?
82420.e: In the closed bottle the gas is under pressure. When you open it, some of it rushes out with a hiss.
82420.m: A fizzy bottle hisses when opened.

82421.q: Is there spring water that is naturally fizzy?
82421.e: Some water takes up carbon dioxide deep underground. In Switzerland there are such springs, for example, in the Lower Engadine near Scuol.
82421.m: Some mineral springs are naturally fizzy.

82422.q: What is a device called that makes tap water fizzy at home?
82422.e: A sparkling water maker presses carbon dioxide from a gas canister into the water. This makes bubbles.
82422.m: With a sparkling water maker you can make fizzy water yourself.

82423.q: What does fizzy mineral water feel like in your mouth?
82423.e: The little gas bubbles burst on your tongue. You feel this as a tingle.

82424.q: What can a paper coffee filter take out of dirty water?
82424.e: Grains of sand are too big for the tiny holes in the paper. They get caught in the filter.
82424.m: A paper filter holds back sand.

82425.q: Can a paper filter take the salt out of salt water?
82425.e: Dissolved salt has broken up into tiny particles. These fit through every hole in the paper.
82425.m: Dissolved substances cannot simply be filtered out.

82426.q: Which layers are often used for a home-made water filter?
82426.e: The coarse gravel holds back big pieces, the sand smaller ones. The cotton wool catches the fine bits left over.
82426.m: Gravel, sand and cotton wool make cloudy water clearer.

82427.q: Which kind of carbon is found in many water filters?
82427.e: Activated carbon has a huge number of tiny pores. Smells and tastes get stuck to them.

82428.q: How is rainwater cleaned in nature before it becomes groundwater?
a: It seeps through gravel and sand
82428.e: On its way through soil, sand and gravel, a lot of dirt gets caught. The ground acts like a big filter.

82429.q: What is a plant called that turns lake water into drinking water?
82429.e: In a lake water works, water from the lake is filtered and cleaned. Zurich and Geneva, for example, get part of their drinking water this way.
82429.m: A lake water works turns lake water into drinking water.

82430.q: What does a tea strainer hold back?
82430.e: The hot water flows through the tiny holes. The tea leaves stay in the strainer.
82430.m: A tea strainer holds back the leaves.

82431.q: Why does a simple sand filter not make stream water safe to drink?
a: The sand makes the water salty
The water disappears into the sand
82431.e: A simple filter makes the water clearer. But it cannot reliably hold back very small germs.
82431.m: Clear water is not always clean drinking water.

82432.q: Which of these objects floats on water?
82432.e: Cork is very light and full of tiny air pockets. That is why a cork floats on top.
82432.m: A cork always floats on top.

82433.q: Why can a big steel ship float?
a: It is full of air inside
82433.e: A lump of steel would sink. But a ship is hollow and pushes aside a lot of water, so the water carries it.

82434.q: What helps small children stay up when learning to swim?
82434.e: Armbands are filled with air. They hold up the arms and so keep the child at the surface.

82435.q: What is the force with which water pushes things upwards called?
82435.e: Water pushes from below against everything in it. This force is called buoyancy.
82435.m: Buoyancy pushes things in water upwards.

82436.q: What happens if you shape a sinking ball of modelling clay into a flat little boat?
82436.e: As a boat, the clay pushes aside much more water. So the buoyancy is enough to carry it.
82436.m: Shape helps decide whether something floats.

82437.q: Why can you lie on the surface of the Dead Sea almost without moving?
82437.e: The Dead Sea contains much more salt than other seas. This water holds up the body especially well.
82437.m: In the Dead Sea you float like a cork.

82438.q: Which animals often have a swim bladder to hover in the water?
82438.e: Many fish have a gas-filled swim bladder in their belly. With it they hover in the water without sinking.
82438.m: The swim bladder helps fish hover.

82439.q: What does an apple do when you put it in a bucket of water?
82439.e: An apple contains a lot of air between its cells. That is why it floats on top.

82440.q: Why do children wear a life jacket on a boat?
a: It keeps their head above water
It protects them from the sun
82440.e: If you fall into the water, the life jacket holds you up. This keeps your head above the surface.
82440.m: A life jacket keeps you above water.

82441.q: What do you call a mixture in which a substance is completely dissolved in water?
82441.e: When sugar or salt has completely disappeared into water, a clear solution forms. You can no longer see any grains in it.
82441.m: A dissolved substance and water make a solution.

82442.q: Why can't you see dissolved sugar in water any more?
a: It has broken up into tiny particles
It has flown into the air
82442.e: The sugar is still there, but it has broken up into particles so small that you cannot see them.
82442.m: Dissolved sugar is invisible, but still there.

82443.q: What happens when you pour squash into water and stir?
82443.e: When stirred, squash spreads evenly through the water. The whole drink becomes sweet and coloured.

82444.q: What does water with a lot of salt dissolved in it look like?
82444.e: Dissolved salt particles are so small that light gets through. The salt water looks like normal water.
82444.m: Salt water looks like pure water.

82445.q: What is the liquid called in which a substance dissolves, for example water in sugar water?
82445.e: The water dissolves the sugar. That is why it is called a solvent.
82445.m: Water is the most important solvent.

82446.q: What happens to a sugar cube in cold water if you don't stir?
82446.e: The sugar dissolves even without stirring. But it takes much longer.
82446.m: Sugar dissolves even without stirring, just more slowly.

82447.q: Does a glass of water get heavier if you dissolve salt in it?
a: Yes, the salt is still in it
82447.e: The salt has only broken up into tiny particles. It is still in the water and weighs just as much as before.

a: Water with dissolved substances from leaves
82448.e: In hot water, colour, scent and flavour dissolve out of the leaves. The leaves themselves are left behind.
82448.m: Tea contains dissolved substances from leaves.

82449.q: Can you drink water from the tap in Switzerland?
82449.e: Tap water in Switzerland is strictly checked. You can drink it without worrying.
82449.m: Swiss tap water is good drinking water.

82450.q: What does the sign ‘Not drinking water’ on a fountain mean?
a: You should not drink the water
82450.e: At some fountains the water is not checked as drinking water. The sign warns you not to drink it.
82450.m: If it says ‘Not drinking water’, don't drink from the fountain.

82451.q: Why can't you simply drink seawater?
82451.e: Seawater contains a great deal of salt. If you drink it, you get even thirstier.
82451.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

82452.q: Which Swiss city is known for over 1200 public fountains?
82452.e: The city of Zurich has over 1200 fountains. Fresh drinking water flows from most of them.
82452.m: Zurich is a city of fountains.

82453.q: Which drink is the best thirst quencher?
82453.e: Water quenches your thirst and has no sugar. Sweet drinks should only be drunk now and then.
82453.m: Water is the best thirst quencher.

82454.q: What is the water that comes out of the tap at home called?
82454.e: The water flows through pipes all the way to your home and out of the tap. That is why it is called tap water.
82454.m: Tap water comes out of the tap.

82455.q: What is the large store in which drinking water for a village is collected called?
82455.e: In the reservoir, clean drinking water is stored, often on a hill. From there it flows under pressure into the houses.

82456.q: What does it mean when people say the drinking water is ‘hard’?
a: It contains a lot of lime
82456.e: Hard water contains a lot of dissolved lime from the ground. You can see this from white marks in the basin or the kettle.
82456.m: Hard water contains a lot of lime.

82457.q: What must you never put into a socket?
82457.e: There is dangerous electricity in the socket. If you put metal into it, the current can flow through your body, and that can kill you.
82457.m: Only a matching plug belongs in a socket.

82458.q: What are child safety covers in sockets for?
a: So children cannot put anything in
82458.e: A child safety cover closes the holes of the socket. Only a proper plug can open it.
82458.m: Child safety covers protect small children from electricity.

82459.q: How many holes does a normal Swiss socket have for a plug?
82459.e: Swiss sockets have three holes, one of them for the earth wire. Two-pin plugs still fit in them.
82459.m: A Swiss socket has three holes.

82460.q: How do you pull a plug out of a socket correctly?
82460.e: If you yank the cable, you can damage the wires inside. That is why you always hold the plug.
82460.m: Always pull the plug, never the cable.

82461.q: Why should you never plug in devices with wet hands?
82461.e: Water conducts electricity. With wet hands, the current can get into your body more easily.
82461.m: Electricity and water are a dangerous mix.

82462.q: What is a device with several sockets on one cable called?
82462.e: You can connect several devices at once to a multi-socket extension lead. But you must not overload it.
82462.m: A multi-socket extension lead has several sockets.

82463.q: What do you often need on holiday abroad, because the sockets look different there?
82463.e: In many countries, Swiss plugs do not fit the sockets. A travel adaptor connects plug and socket.
82463.m: A travel adaptor helps with foreign sockets.

82464.q: Who is allowed to connect new sockets in a house?
82464.e: Work on electrical wiring is dangerous. That is why connecting new sockets is left to a trained electrician.
82464.m: New sockets are connected by a qualified person.

82465.q: What voltage does an ordinary small AA battery have?
82465.e: An AA battery supplies 1.5 volts. This small voltage is harmless to people.
82465.m: A small AA battery has 1.5 volts.

82466.q: What are the two ends of a battery called?
82466.e: A battery has a positive terminal and a negative terminal. The current flows through the device from one terminal to the other.
82466.m: Every battery has a positive and a negative terminal.

82467.q: Where do you take empty batteries in Switzerland?
a: Back to the shop or to a collection point
82467.e: Wherever batteries are sold, empty ones are taken back free of charge. Valuable materials are recovered from them.
82467.m: Take empty batteries to a collection point.

82468.q: Why do batteries not belong in the normal rubbish?
a: They contain substances that harm the environment
They are too heavy for the bag
82468.e: Batteries contain metals and other substances. These should not get into the environment and can be recycled.
82468.m: Batteries do not belong in the rubbish.

82469.q: Where does the electricity in a battery come from?
82469.e: Inside the battery, substances react with each other. In this process, chemical energy becomes electrical energy.
82469.m: In a battery, chemical energy becomes electricity.

82470.q: Which battery is inside many wristwatches?
82470.e: A button cell is small and flat like a button. It fits well into watches and small devices.
82470.m: Watches often run on a button cell.

82471.q: Which battery is shaped like a small block with two snap connectors on top?
82471.e: The block battery supplies 9 volts. Its two terminals sit side by side on the top.
82471.m: The 9-volt battery has both terminals on top.

82472.q: Why must button cells be kept away from small children?
82472.e: A swallowed button cell can cause serious injuries inside the body. Then you must go to the doctor straight away.
82472.m: Button cells do not belong in children’s hands.

82473.q: What usually happens if you put a battery into a device the wrong way round?
a: The device lights up in colours
82473.e: Plus and minus must be the right way round. Otherwise the current cannot flow properly through the device.
82473.m: When putting in batteries, check plus and minus.

82474.q: What is needed for a lamp to light up on a battery?
82474.e: The current must be able to flow from the battery through the lamp and back again. This is called a closed circuit.
82474.m: Current only flows in a closed circuit.

82475.q: What happens to the lamp if you disconnect a wire in the circuit?
82475.e: If a wire is disconnected, the circuit is broken. The current can no longer flow, and the lamp goes out.
82475.m: A broken circuit makes the lamp go out.

82476.q: Which of these objects does not conduct electricity?
82476.e: Paper clips, nails and coins are made of metal and conduct electricity. Rubber does not let current through.
82476.m: Metal conducts electricity, rubber does not.

82477.q: What do you call materials that do not let electricity through, such as plastic or glass?
82477.e: Insulators do not let any current through. They are needed wherever the current should not reach.

82478.q: What switches off the electricity in a house when too much current flows?
82478.e: The fuse in the fuse box breaks the circuit when there is danger. That way it protects against fires.
82478.m: The fuse protects the house from too much current.

82479.q: Where in nature are there huge electric sparks?
82479.e: Lightning is a gigantic electric spark between a cloud and the ground. That is why you look for shelter in a building during a thunderstorm.
82479.m: Lightning is a huge electric spark.

82480.q: Two little bulbs are connected one after the other to the same battery. What happens if you unscrew one?
82480.e: With bulbs connected one after the other, there is only one path for the current. If one bulb is missing, the whole circuit is broken.
82480.m: In a series circuit, all the bulbs go out together.

82481.q: What does a yellow warning triangle with a black lightning bolt mean?
82481.e: This sign hangs, for example, on electricity boxes and transformer stations. It warns of dangerous electrical voltage.
82481.m: The lightning sign warns of electricity.

82482.q: What happens when you press the light switch?
a: The lamp goes on or off
82482.e: The switch lets the current flow to the lamp or stops it. That is why the light goes on or off.
82482.m: You turn the light on and off with the light switch.

82483.q: What is a switch that lets you make the light brighter and dimmer called?
82483.e: With a dimmer you can smoothly change the brightness of a lamp. That way you can match the light to the mood.
82483.m: You adjust the brightness with a dimmer.

82484.q: What is a device that switches the light on by itself when someone moves called?
82484.e: A motion sensor senses when someone comes near and then switches the light on. You often find one by front doors.
82484.m: A motion sensor switches on the light when there is movement.

82485.q: Why does the light in the stairwell often go off by itself after a few minutes?
a: So the lamp can cool down
82485.e: A timer switch turns the light off after a set time. That way it does not stay on for hours when nobody is there.
82485.m: A timer switch helps save electricity.

82486.q: Why do some light switches glow faintly in the dark?
a: So you can find them more easily
82486.e: A tiny lamp in the switch shows where it is in a dark room. So you do not have to feel along the wall for long.
82486.m: You can find glowing switches even in the dark.

82487.q: Can you switch the same lamp on and off with two switches at different ends of a corridor?
82487.e: With two-way switching you can switch the light at both ends of a corridor or staircase. That is very handy.
82487.m: With two switches you can switch a lamp from two places.

82488.q: What is a switch that only gives current as long as you press it, for example on a doorbell, called?
82488.e: A push button springs back as soon as you let go. That is why the doorbell only rings as long as you press it.
82488.m: A push button only works while you press it.

82489.q: What do you do if wires are sticking out of a light switch?
a: Do not touch them and fetch an adult
Clean them with a wet cloth
82489.e: Loose wires can be live. That is why you do not touch them and get help straight away.

82490.q: Why is an electric cable covered in plastic on the outside?
a: The plastic protects against electric shocks
82490.e: Inside are wires that the current flows through. The plastic covering stops you from touching the current.
82490.m: The covering of a cable protects you from electricity.

82491.q: What do you do with a device whose cable is damaged?
82491.e: With a damaged cable you can get an electric shock. The device must be repaired or replaced.
82491.m: Do not use devices with a broken cable.

82492.q: Why should you not lay electric cables under a carpet or trap them in doors?
a: They can get damaged and overheat
82492.e: A trapped cable can break inside. Then it can get hot and even start a fire.
82492.m: Cables need room and must not be trapped.

82493.q: What are the tall structures that carry power lines across the country called?
82493.e: Electricity pylons hold the lines high above the ground. That way electricity can get from the power station to the towns.
82493.m: Pylons carry power lines across the country.

82494.q: Why do you never fly a kite near power lines?
a: There is a deadly danger from electricity
The kite flies too fast there
The line takes away the wind
The birds get in the way there
82494.e: If the kite gets caught in a line, the current can flow down the string to the person. That can kill.
82494.m: Fly kites far away from power lines.

82495.q: What makes climbing onto a parked railway carriage deadly dangerous?
82495.e: The railway’s overhead line carries 15,000 volts. The current can jump across even if you only come close to the line.
82495.m: Keep away from railway carriages and overhead lines.

82496.q: What is a cable that lets a device stand further away from the socket called?
82496.e: An extension lead has a plug at one end and a socket at the other. That way the electricity reaches further.
82496.m: An extension lead takes the electricity further.

82497.q: Why should you unroll a cable reel completely before plugging in a powerful device?
82497.e: A rolled-up cable cannot give off its heat. With powerful devices it can overheat.
82497.m: Always unroll a cable reel completely.

82498.q: Where do you often see solar cells on houses?
82498.e: On the roof, the solar cells get a lot of sunlight. They do not bother anyone there either.
82498.m: Solar cells belong in a sunny spot.

82499.q: What do you call lots of solar cells sitting together on one panel?
82499.e: A single solar cell only supplies a little electricity. That is why many are joined together to make a solar module.
82499.m: Lots of solar cells make a solar module.

82500.q: When does a solar cell produce the most electricity?
a: At midday on a sunny day
In the middle of the night
82500.e: The more sunlight falls on the cell, the more electricity it produces. At midday the Sun is at its highest.
82500.m: Lots of sun means lots of solar power.

82501.q: Which small device often has a tiny solar cell?
82501.e: Some calculators need so little electricity that a small solar cell is enough. They then work without a battery.

82502.q: What colour are solar cells usually?
82502.e: Dark surfaces absorb a lot of light. That is why solar cells are usually dark blue or black.
82502.m: Solar cells are dark so they absorb a lot of light.

82503.q: On which mountain in the Bernese Jura has a well-known solar power station stood since 1992?
82503.e: The Mont-Soleil solar power station was one of the first large solar plants in Switzerland. The name “Soleil” means sun in French.
82503.m: On Mont-Soleil, electricity is made from the sun.

82504.q: Which direction is best for solar cells to face in Switzerland?
82504.e: Here, the Sun is in the south at midday. That is why south-facing solar cells get the most light.
82504.m: In Switzerland, solar cells work best facing south.

82505.q: What happens to solar power from the roof that the family does not need right now?
a: It flows into the grid or into a battery
It turns into heat in the roof
82505.e: Surplus electricity can flow into the public grid and be used by others. Or it can be stored in a battery in the house.
82505.m: Surplus solar power is shared or stored.

82506.q: What makes a wind turbine turn?
82506.e: The wind pushes against the blades and turns them. A generator inside turns this into electricity.
82506.m: A wind turbine makes electricity from wind.

82507.q: How many blades do most large wind turbines have?
82507.e: Almost all modern large wind turbines have three rotor blades. That way they turn calmly and evenly.
82507.m: Large wind turbines usually have three blades.

82508.q: Where is the largest wind farm in Switzerland?
a: On Mont-Crosin in the Bernese Jura
On the shore of Lake Geneva
82508.e: The first wind turbines were built on Mont-Crosin in 1996. Today 16 turbines turn there; it is the largest wind farm in Switzerland.
82508.m: Mont-Crosin is Switzerland’s best-known wind farm.

82509.q: Why are wind turbines often put on hills and ridges?
a: The wind blows more strongly there
82509.e: High up and on open ridges, the wind blows more strongly and steadily. That way the wind turbines produce more electricity.
82509.m: Wind turbines need places with lots of wind.

82510.q: What were windmills mainly used for in the past?
82510.e: The sails of the windmill turned heavy millstones. These were used to grind grain into flour.
82510.m: Windmills used to grind grain into flour.

82511.q: Why are wind turbines stopped in a very violent storm?
a: So they do not get damaged
So they can sleep at night
82511.e: In winds that are too strong, the blades could turn too fast. That is why they are stopped for protection.
82511.m: In storms, wind turbines are stopped for protection.

82512.q: Which toy turns like a little wind turbine when you blow on it?
82512.e: The pinwheel has light blades that even a breath can turn. It works like a big wind turbine.
82512.m: A pinwheel turns in the wind.

82513.q: On which Alpine pass have five large wind turbines been turning since 2020?
82513.e: In 2020 a wind farm with five turbines started operating near the Gotthard Hospice. It lies more than 2,000 metres above sea level.
82513.m: Wind power is made on the Gotthard too.

82514.q: What provides the power for a hydroelectric power station?
82514.e: The water rushes through the power station with great force. Its movement is turned into electricity.
82514.m: A hydroelectric power station makes electricity from moving water.

82515.q: What turns in a hydroelectric power station when the water rushes onto it?
82515.e: The water drives a turbine, similar to a paddle wheel. The turbine turns a generator that produces electricity.
82515.m: In the power station, water turns a turbine.

82516.q: Why is a large storage lake in the mountains useful for the electricity supply?
a: It holds water ready until electricity is needed
It holds the glaciers in place
82516.e: In summer, lots of meltwater is collected. In winter, when more electricity is needed, it is let through the power station.
82516.m: A storage lake saves water for later.

82517.q: How does the water get from the storage lake down to the power station in the valley?
a: Through thick pipes in the mountain
82517.e: The water shoots down the mountain through thick pipes or tunnels. At the bottom it drives the turbines with great force.
82517.m: Thick pipes carry the water to the power station.

82518.q: Where are run-of-river power stations located?
82518.e: Run-of-river power stations use the water that constantly flows in a river. Many are on the Rhine and the Aare, for example.
82518.m: Run-of-river power stations are on rivers.

82519.q: Where does the water in Alpine reservoirs mainly come from?
82519.e: In spring and summer, snow and glacier ice melt. The meltwater fills the reservoirs.
82519.m: Meltwater fills the reservoirs in the mountains.

82520.q: What was a mill by a stream, where the water turned a big wheel, called?
82520.e: The flowing water turned the mill wheel. That way grain could be ground or wood sawn without muscle power.
82520.m: Water mills used the power of water long ago.

82521.q: Why are fish ladders built at river power stations?
a: So fish can swim past the power station
So people can climb into the water
82521.e: Many fish migrate upstream. Using the fish ladder made of small pools, they get past the power station.
82521.m: Fish ladders help fish past obstacles.

82522.q: What should you do when you leave a room?
82522.e: Light in an empty room uses electricity without being useful. That is why you switch it off when you go out.
82522.m: Switch off the light when you leave the room.

82523.q: How do you save electricity with the TV?
a: Switch it off completely instead of standby
Leave it on all the time
82523.e: Even on standby, a device uses some electricity. Switching it off completely saves energy.
82523.m: Switching off saves more electricity than standby.

82524.q: Why should you not leave the fridge door open for long?
82524.e: When the door is open, warm air flows in. The fridge then has to cool for longer and uses more electricity.
82524.m: A closed fridge door saves electricity.

82525.q: What normally uses less hot water?
82525.e: A full bath needs much more hot water than a short shower. Heating water takes energy.

82526.q: What is the most energy-saving way to air a room in winter?
a: Briefly, with the window wide open
For hours with the window tilted
82526.e: When you air a room briefly with the window wide open, fresh air comes in fast, but the walls do not cool down. A tilted window loses a lot of heat.
82526.m: In winter, air rooms briefly and thoroughly.

82527.q: What is the coloured label that shows how economical a device is called?
82527.e: The energy label uses letters and colours to show how much energy a device uses. Green means economical.
82527.m: The energy label shows how economical a device is.

82528.q: How does washing dry without any electricity?
82528.e: On the line, sun and air dry the washing. A tumble dryer, on the other hand, uses a lot of electricity.
82528.m: The washing line needs no electricity.

82529.q: What do you do with the charger when the mobile phone is full?
82529.e: Some chargers use a little electricity even without a phone. That is why you unplug them after charging.

82530.q: What is the dynamo on a bike for?
a: It makes electricity for the lights
82530.e: The dynamo is driven by the turning wheel. It produces electricity for the bike lights.
82530.m: The dynamo makes electricity for the bike lights.

82531.q: Where does the bike dynamo get its energy from?
82531.e: Pedalling turns the wheel. The dynamo uses this movement to make electricity.
82531.m: With a dynamo, your legs make the electricity.

82532.q: What does a bike light with a standlight do when you stop at a junction?
a: It keeps shining for a while
82532.e: A small store in the lamp is charged while you ride. When you stop, it keeps the lamp shining for a few minutes.
82532.m: The standlight keeps shining when you stop.

82533.q: Where on a bike is a hub dynamo fitted?
a: In the middle of the front wheel
82533.e: The hub dynamo sits in the hub, in other words in the middle of the front wheel. It runs quietly and reliably, even in the rain.
82533.m: A hub dynamo sits in the middle of the wheel.

82534.q: Do you have to pedal a bit harder with the dynamo switched on?
a: No, you do not have to pedal at all
82534.e: The dynamo needs energy to make electricity. This energy comes from your legs, so pedalling is a bit harder.
82534.m: A dynamo needs a little leg power.

82535.q: What colour must the light at the front of a bike be?
82535.e: At the front, the bike light shines white so you can see the way and be seen. A different light shines towards the back.
82535.m: The front bike light is white.

82536.q: Why do people like to ride a bike with lights on even during the day?
82536.e: With lights, cyclists catch drivers’ attention sooner. That makes the road safer.
82536.m: Lights on your bike make you easier to see.

82537.q: What does a dynamo on a bike do?
a: It makes electricity for the light while you ride
It stores water for the ride
82537.e: The wheel turns a magnet inside the dynamo. This produces electricity that makes the lamp shine. The faster you ride, the brighter the light.
82537.m: A bike dynamo turns movement into electricity.

82538.q: What is inside a torch so that it shines?
82538.e: Batteries or a rechargeable battery supply the electricity for the lamp. That is why you can take it anywhere without a cable.
82538.m: A torch gets its electricity from batteries.

82539.q: What gives off the light in most modern torches?
82539.e: LED stands for light-emitting diode. It uses little electricity and lasts a very long time.

82540.q: Why does a torch shine more weakly after a long time?
82540.e: Batteries give off their energy bit by bit. When they are almost empty, the light gets weaker.
82540.m: A weak light shows the batteries are almost empty.

82541.q: How does a wind-up torch with a crank work?
a: You make the electricity by turning
You put it in the socket
82541.e: Inside the torch is a small generator. When you turn the crank, electricity is produced, with no battery at all.
82541.m: A wind-up torch makes its own electricity.

82542.q: What is a lamp you wear on your head with a strap called?
82542.e: A head torch always shines where you are looking. That way you have both hands free, for example when camping.
82542.m: With a head torch your hands are free.

82543.q: How many times a minute do you give a light signal in the alpine distress signal?
82543.e: In the alpine distress signal, you give six signals a minute, then pause for a minute. The reply is three signals a minute.
82543.m: The alpine distress signal is six signals a minute.

82544.q: Why does a torch belong in the emergency supplies at home?
82544.e: If the power goes off, the lights in the house stay dark. With a torch and batteries you can still see.
82544.m: A torch helps in a power cut.

82545.q: What does the shiny mirror behind the bulb of a torch do?
82545.e: The mirror is called a reflector. It throws the light forwards, creating a bright beam.
82545.m: The reflector focuses the light forwards.

82546.q: Why should you never shine a bright torch into someone’s eyes?
a: It dazzles and can harm the eyes
It empties the battery at once
82546.e: Very bright light dazzles, and afterwards you cannot see well for a while. Strong lamps can even harm the eyes.
82546.m: Never shine a light into someone’s eyes.

82547.q: What can a rechargeable battery do that a normal battery cannot?
82547.e: A rechargeable battery stores electricity and can be charged again many times. A normal battery runs flat and must then be disposed of.
82547.m: A rechargeable battery can be charged again and again.

82548.q: What do you use to charge a mobile phone’s battery?
82548.e: The charger takes electricity from the socket and passes it to the battery in a suitable form. There it is stored.
82548.m: You charge a mobile phone with a charger.

82549.q: What does the battery symbol at the top of the phone screen show?
82549.e: The fuller the symbol, the more charge is left in the battery. When it is almost empty, you should charge the phone.
82549.m: The battery symbol shows the charge level.

82550.q: Why should you not leave a phone or battery in a hot car in the sun?
82550.e: Great heat wears batteries out faster. In the worst case they can even become dangerous.
82550.m: Batteries do not like great heat.

82551.q: Which bike has a battery that helps when you pedal?
82551.e: On an e-bike, an electric motor powered by the battery helps drive the bike. That makes it easier to get up hills.
82551.m: An e-bike rides with the help of a battery.

82552.q: What do you do if a rechargeable battery is fat and swollen?
a: Stop using it and hand it in
82552.e: A swollen battery is damaged and can catch fire. You take it to a specialist shop or a collection point.
82552.m: Do not use swollen batteries any more.

82553.q: What happens to a mobile phone when the battery is completely empty?
82553.e: Without electricity from the battery, the phone cannot work. Only after charging can it be switched on again.
82553.m: When the battery is empty, the phone switches off.

82554.q: What do you call it when you simply lay a phone on a flat charging pad to charge it?
82554.e: With wireless charging, the energy flows from the charging pad into the phone without a plug. The phone has to lie exactly right on the pad.
82554.m: Some phones can charge without a cable.

a: A portable battery for charging on the go
82555.e: A power bank stores electricity. With it you can charge your phone on the go without a socket.
82555.m: With a power bank you can charge on the go.

82556.q: How many different digits are there in our number system?
82556.e: Our number system is a base-ten system. All numbers are written with ten different digits.
82556.m: We write all numbers with ten digits.

82557.e: 9 is the largest digit. 10 is already a number made of two digits.

82558.q: How many digits does the number 365 have?
82558.e: The number 365 is made of the digits 3, 6 and 5. That is three digits.

82559.q: Which digit is in the tens place in the number 47?
82559.e: In 47, the 4 stands for 4 tens and the 7 for 7 ones.
82559.m: In 47, the 4 is the tens digit.

82560.q: Which digit is in the ones place in the number 582?
82560.e: The ones place is on the far right. In 582, that is the 2.
82560.m: The ones place is on the far right.

82561.q: Where do our digits originally come from?
82561.e: Our digits were invented in India. They came to Europe through Arab scholars, which is why they are called Arabic numerals.
82561.m: Our digits originally come from India.

82562.q: How many different digits do you need to write the number 1111?
82562.e: The number 1111 is made of the digit 1 four times. So you only need one single digit.
82562.m: A number can contain the same digit several times.

82563.q: Which digit appears twice in the number 2026?
82563.e: The number 2026 is made of the digits 2, 0, 2 and 6. The 2 appears twice.

82564.q: Which number can you make with the digits 3 and 8 if it should be as large as possible?
82564.e: The larger digit goes at the front, in the tens place. That gives 83.
82564.m: The larger digit goes at the front.

82565.e: If you add zero, the number stays the same. 7 + 0 makes 7.
82565.m: Adding zero does not change a number.

82566.e: Any number times zero makes zero. Five times nothing is nothing.

82567.e: When you count backwards, 0 comes after 1.

82568.e: If you take exactly 9 away from 9, nothing is left. The answer is 0.
82568.m: A number minus itself makes zero.

82569.q: Which old number symbols had no zero?
82569.e: The Romans wrote numbers with letters such as I, V and X. They had no symbol for zero.
82569.m: The Romans had no symbol for zero.

82570.q: How many zeros does the number 100 have?
82570.e: The number 100 is written with a 1 and two zeros.

82571.q: What happens to the number 6 if you add a zero on the right?
82571.e: If you add a zero, the number becomes ten times as big. 6 becomes 60.
82571.m: Adding a zero makes a number ten times bigger.

82572.e: The smallest digit is 0. It stands for nothing.

82573.e: An abacus is a calculating tool with beads on rods. You slide the beads to count and calculate.
82573.m: You can do sums with an abacus.

82574.q: What do you slide back and forth on an abacus?
82574.e: On an abacus, beads are threaded onto rods or wires. You slide them back and forth.
82574.m: On an abacus you slide beads.

82575.q: How many beads per row does a school counting frame often have?
82575.e: A counting frame for children usually has ten rows of ten beads each. That fits our base-ten system.
82575.m: A school counting frame usually has ten beads per row.

82576.q: How many beads does a counting frame with 10 rows of 10 beads have?
82576.e: 10 rows of 10 beads make 10 times 10, so 100 beads.
82576.m: Ten times ten makes a hundred.

82577.q: Is the abacus a new or a very old invention?
a: It was invented ten years ago
82577.e: People were already calculating with the abacus well over a thousand years ago, for example in China and Japan.
82577.m: The abacus is a very old calculating tool.

82578.q: Does an abacus need electricity or batteries?
82578.e: The abacus works only with your hands. It is much older than any battery.

82579.q: Which device has mostly replaced the abacus in everyday life?
82579.e: Today most people calculate with a calculator or a mobile phone. In the past, people often used the abacus.
82579.m: The calculator has mostly replaced the abacus.

82580.q: On a counting frame, 3 beads are on the left and 4 more beads are pushed over. How many are there altogether?
82580.e: 3 beads and 4 beads make 3 + 4 together, so 7 beads.

82581.q: How many items are in a dozen?
82581.e: A dozen means twelve items. In the past, eggs were often counted in dozens.

82582.q: How many items are in half a dozen?
82582.e: A dozen is 12 items. Half of that is 6.
82582.m: Half a dozen is six items.

82583.q: How many eggs are two dozen eggs?
82583.e: A dozen is 12. Two dozen are 12 + 12, so 24.

82584.q: How many eggs are a dozen?
82584.e: A dozen is 12 items. That is why many egg boxes hold exactly 12 eggs.

82585.e: A dozen is 12 eggs. 12 + 12 + 12 makes 36, so it is 3 dozen.

82587.q: A box for a dozen eggs has 9 eggs in it. How many are missing?
82587.e: A dozen is 12 eggs. 12 − 9 makes 3, so 3 eggs are missing.
82587.m: With nine eggs, three are still missing from a dozen.

82588.q: A baker adds one extra bread roll free to a dozen rolls. How many rolls are there now?
82588.e: A dozen is 12 rolls. With one more roll it is 12 + 1 = 13. This is called a baker’s dozen.
82588.m: A baker’s dozen is thirteen items.

82589.q: How many socks are a pair of socks?
82589.e: A pair is always two things that belong together.

82590.q: How many hands do 4 children have altogether?
82590.e: Each child has a pair of hands, so 2. 4 times 2 makes 8 hands.

82591.q: Which things do you usually buy as a pair?
82591.e: You need gloves for both hands. That is why they come as a pair.
82591.m: You buy gloves as a pair.

82592.q: A beetle has three pairs of legs. How many legs is that?
82592.e: A pair is two legs. 3 times 2 makes 6 legs.

82594.q: Every child has a pair of ears. How many ears do 3 children have altogether?
82594.e: A pair is two ears. 3 times 2 makes 6 ears.
82594.m: We have a pair of ears.

82595.q: 7 children line up in twos. How many children are left on their own?
82595.e: 7 children make 3 pairs, which is 6 children. One child is left on their own.
82595.m: With an odd number, one is left over when you make pairs.

82596.q: In the card game pairs (Memory), what do you call two cards with the same picture?
82596.e: In pairs, you look for two matching cards. Two things that belong together are called a pair.
82596.m: In the game pairs, you look for matching pairs.

82597.q: Into how many halves is a domino divided?
82597.e: A domino has two halves. Each half has dots or no dot.

82598.q: How many tiles does a normal set of dominoes with at most 6 dots per half have?
82598.e: The usual set goes up to double six. Each combination appears once, which makes 28 tiles.
82598.m: A normal set of dominoes has 28 tiles.

82599.q: How many dots does the double-six domino have altogether?
82599.e: On the double six, each half has 6 dots. 6 + 6 makes 12 dots.
82599.m: The double-six domino has twelve dots.

82600.q: Which number does an empty half of a domino show?
82600.e: An empty half has no dots. It stands for the number zero.
82600.m: An empty domino half means zero.

82601.q: A domino has 2 and 5 dots. How many dots is that altogether?
82601.e: You add both halves together: 2 + 5 makes 7.

82602.q: In dominoes, which tile fits next to a half with 4 dots?
82602.e: In dominoes, you put halves with the same number of dots next to each other. Only a 4 fits next to a 4.
82602.m: In dominoes, you match the same numbers.

82603.q: In the domino effect, what happens when you push the first domino?
a: They all fall one after another
82603.e: When dominoes stand in a row, each falling domino pushes the next one. So they all fall over one after another.
82603.m: In the domino effect, one domino falls after another.

82604.q: How many dots does a domino with 3 and 3 dots have?
82604.e: Both halves have 3 dots. 3 + 3 makes 6 dots.

82607.e: “Thirty” means three tens, so 30. The number 13 is called “thirteen”.

82609.e: The number 1000 is called “a thousand”. It has three zeros.
82609.m: The number 1000 is called a thousand.

82610.q: How do you say the number 3 in French?
82610.e: In French you count un, deux, trois. So 3 is called “trois”.

82611.q: How do you say the number 5 in English?
82611.e: In English, the number 5 is called “five”.

82612.q: In a race, only one child finishes before Tim. Which place does Tim come?
82612.e: The first child to finish comes first. Tim comes straight after, so he is in second place. For places you need ordinal numbers.
82612.m: For places you need ordinal numbers.

82613.q: How many zeros does a million have?
82613.e: A million is written 1,000,000. That is six zeros.

82614.q: How do you write a million in digits?
82614.e: A million is a 1 with six zeros. It is written 1,000,000.

82615.q: In Switzerland, how are large numbers like 1'000'000 often separated when written?
82615.e: In Switzerland, people often put an apostrophe between each group of three digits. That makes large numbers easier to read.
82615.m: In Switzerland, thousands are often separated with an apostrophe.

82617.q: How much are two half millions together?
82617.e: Half a million is 500,000. Two of them make 1,000,000, which is one million.

82618.q: What is the number you get from a thousand million called?
82618.e: A thousand million make a billion. It has nine zeros.
82618.m: A thousand million is a billion.

82619.e: A millionaire owns at least a million francs or another currency. That is a lot of money.
82619.m: A millionaire owns at least a million.

82620.q: Which place in the rankings is the winner?
82620.e: In a ranking list, the best person is right at the top in 1st place.

82621.q: Which medal does second place get at the Olympic Games?
82621.e: Second place gets a silver medal. The winner gets gold.

82622.q: Which medal does third place get at the Olympic Games?
82622.e: Third place gets a bronze medal.

82623.q: How many people stand on a winners’ podium?
82623.e: The three best stand on the podium: 1st place in the middle, 2nd and 3rd place beside it.
82623.m: The three best stand on the podium.

82624.e: In a ski race, whoever takes the least time wins. The shortest time comes 1st.
82624.m: In a ski race, the shortest time wins.

82625.q: Anna has 8 points, Ben 5 points and Chiara 10 points. Who is in 1st place?
82625.e: Whoever has the most points is at the front. 10 points are more than 8 and 5.
82625.m: With points, whoever has the most wins.

82626.q: Lea has 7 points, Tim 4 points and Noah 9 points. Who is in last place?
82626.e: Tim has the fewest with 4 points. So he is in last place.
82626.m: Whoever has the fewest points is at the back.

82627.q: Which place comes straight after 4th place in a ranking?
82627.e: Places are counted in order. After 4th place comes 5th place.

82628.q: Is there a very biggest number of all?
82628.e: You can always add 1 to any number. So there is no biggest number.

82629.q: What does the symbol for infinity look like?
82629.e: The symbol for infinity is ∞. It looks like an 8 lying on its side.
82629.m: The symbol for infinity is an eight lying down.

82630.q: What do the three dots mean in “1, 2, 3, ...”?
82630.e: The three dots show that the sequence goes on. With numbers, it never comes to an end.
82630.m: Three dots after a number sequence mean that it goes on.

82631.e: You add 1 to 1000. That makes 1001. You can always keep counting like this.
82631.m: Every number has a next one.

82632.e: Infinite means that something never stops. It has no end.

82633.q: Are there infinitely many even numbers?
82633.e: After every even number, two steps later there is another even number. That never stops.
82633.m: There are infinitely many even numbers.

82634.q: Can you finish counting to infinity?
82634.e: If you count, you never reach an end, because there is always a next number. Even a computer cannot do it.
82634.m: Nobody can finish counting to infinity.

82635.q: What is bigger than any number you can write down?
82635.e: Every number, even a billion, has an end. Infinity is not an ordinary number; it means that things always go on.
82635.m: Infinity is bigger than any number.

82636.e: The postcode tells the post office which place a letter or parcel should go to.
82636.m: The postcode helps the post office deliver.

82637.e: Bern has the postcode 3000. Postcodes starting with 3 are in the Bern region.

82638.q: Which digit do the postcodes of the city of Zurich start with?
82638.e: The postcodes of the city of Zurich start with 80, for example 8001.

82639.q: Which digit do the postcodes of Geneva and Lausanne start with?
82639.e: In western Switzerland, postcodes start with 1, for example 1201 Geneva.
82639.m: In western Switzerland, postcodes start with 1.

82640.q: Where does the postcode go on a letter in Switzerland?
82640.e: In Switzerland you write the postcode before the town, for example “3000 Bern”.
82640.m: The postcode goes before the town name.

82642.q: Which neighbouring country also uses Swiss postcodes?
82642.e: Liechtenstein is part of the Swiss postcode system. Its postcodes start with 94.

82643.q: Which of these years has a 29 February?
82643.e: 2028 is a leap year. Only leap years have a 29 February.
82643.m: Only leap years have a 29 February.

82644.q: How many years are in a millennium?
82644.e: A millennium lasts a thousand years. We live in the third millennium.
82644.m: A millennium is a thousand years.

82645.q: Roughly how often is there a leap year?
82645.e: Almost always, every fourth year is a leap year. That keeps the calendar in step with the Earth.
82645.m: There is a leap year roughly every four years.

82646.q: Which year is written on the Swiss Federal Charter?
82646.e: The Federal Charter is dated the beginning of August 1291. That is why Switzerland celebrates its national day on 1 August.

82647.q: How many years are in a century?
82647.e: A century lasts 100 years. A decade is 10 years.
82647.m: A century is a hundred years.

82648.q: How many years are in a decade?

82649.e: Each new year is 1 more. 2026 + 1 makes 2027.

82650.q: A child was born in 2018. How old will they be in 2026?
82650.e: You work out 2026 − 2018. That makes 8 years.
82650.m: You work out age with a subtraction.

82651.q: Which digit do the postcodes in Ticino start with?
82651.e: In Ticino, postcodes start with 6, for example 6900 Lugano or 6500 Bellinzona.

82652.q: How many years are there between 2020 and 2026?
82652.e: You work out 2026 − 2020. That makes 6 years.
82652.m: You find the gap between years with subtraction.

82653.q: Who may read your diary if you do not allow it?
82653.e: A diary is part of your privacy. Nobody should read it without your permission.
82653.m: Nobody reads my diary without permission.

82654.q: How can you set who sees your posts in an app?
82654.e: In an app's settings you can often choose who may see something. Best of all, only friends and family.
82654.m: In the settings I decide who sees my things.

82655.q: What does “private” mean for a profile?
82655.e: A private profile can only be seen by people you have allowed. A public profile can be seen by everyone.
82655.m: Only my friends see a private profile.

82656.q: Is it OK to secretly look through another child's phone?
82656.e: Someone else's phone is part of their privacy. You always ask first.
82656.m: I only look at other people's phones with permission.

82657.q: What does “public” mean on the internet?
82657.e: Anyone on the internet can see public posts, strangers included.

82658.q: What should a child do if a game asks for their location?
82658.e: Your location shows where you are right now. Ask your parents first whether the game really needs it.
82658.m: When asked for my location, I ask my parents first.

82659.q: Who else can see a message that you send to lots of people?
82659.e: Anyone who gets a message can read it and forward it. That is why you think carefully first.
82659.m: All the recipients can read a message I send.

82660.q: Can the internet definitely forget something for ever when you delete it?
82660.e: Others may already have copied or saved something before you delete it. That is why the rule is: think first, then post.
82660.m: The internet does not forget so quickly.

82661.q: Which of these is a piece of personal data?
82661.e: Personal data tells something about you as a person. Your address shows where you live.
82661.m: My address is part of my personal data.

82662.q: Who do you give your phone number to on the internet?
82662.e: Your phone number is personal data. Strangers on the internet should not get it.
82662.m: I do not give my phone number to strangers.

82663.q: Which of these is more OK to show in a game?
82663.e: A made-up name says nothing about you. School, address and date of birth are personal data.
82663.m: A made-up name protects me in a game.

82664.q: Why should you not post the name of your school publicly?
82664.e: Anyone who knows the name of your school knows where you are during the day. That is none of a stranger's business.
82664.m: I do not post the name of my school publicly.

82665.q: What do you do if a website asks for your name and address?
82665.e: With personal data you ask your parents first. They know whether the site can be trusted.
82665.m: Before typing in my details, I ask my parents.

82666.q: Which photo gives away where you live?
a: In front of the house with the house number
82666.e: In a photo in front of your house, people might see the street and house number. That way someone could find out where you live.
82666.m: Photos can give away my address too.
